01 · The list

Numbers,
level by level

The number words of Korean from the TOPIK lists: the digits, the tens, hundred, thousand and ten thousand, with the reading and meaning of each. Numbers are the first words that pay for themselves, since prices, dates, times and phone numbers all run on them.

In Lock&Learn Korean these words sit in their level packs (Beginner 1, Beginner 2, Intermediate 1, Intermediate 2 and more), one per glance on the widget: a word waits in hangul with its romanization; one tap reveals the meaning and a real sentence. Beginner 1 is free; every other pack opens with a free preview and another word unlocks daily.

Type to filter by hangul, romanization or meaning. Flashcards hides the meaning until you tap a row; Shuffle deals the list in a new order.

Korean has two number systems and uses both daily. Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이, 삼 …) count money, dates, minutes, phone numbers, floors and anything large. Native Korean numbers (하나, 둘, 셋 …) count things and people with a counter word, and give ages and the hour of the day. "Three o'clock" is 세 시 (native) but "thirty minutes" is 삼십 분 (Sino-Korean).

Sino-Korean numbers stack from the top down: 이십삼 is 23, 삼백 is 300, and Korean groups by ten thousand, so 100,000 is 십만. Native numbers go up to 99 in everyday use (스물 20, 서른 30, 마흔 40, 쉰 50); above that speakers switch to Sino-Korean.

03 · Questions

Asked and
answered

How do I count in Korean?

Start with one to ten from the table, then the tens, hundred and thousand; larger numbers are built by combining them, and the note above the list explains the system. The 58 words here are the number words on the TOPIK vocabulary lists, each with its reading.

Which TOPIK levels are these words from?

48 from TOPIK I, 5 from TOPIK II Intermediate, 5 from TOPIK II Advanced. The level chip on each row says where the word sits, so you can stop at your level or read ahead. Beginner-level words carry a real example sentence; the rest show word, romanization and meaning, with their sentences in the app.

How do I learn numbers words on my iPhone Lock Screen?

Install Lock&Learn Korean, then touch and hold your Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap the widget area and choose Lock&Learn Korean. Enable the level packs these words come from (Beginner 1, Beginner 2, Intermediate 1 and more). A word waits in hangul with its romanization; one tap reveals the meaning and a real sentence.

Is Lock&Learn Korean free?

Yes. The app is free on iOS: Beginner 1 is free, every other pack opens with a free preview, and another word unlocks daily. Lock&Learn+ is an optional upgrade that opens every pack at once, offered as a yearly plan or a one-time lifetime purchase.
